newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Big powers ask Russian standstill for WTO talks.
newsitem.headline: Big powers ask Russian standstill for WTO talks.

text.p: The top four trading powers on Tuesday asked Russia to declare a standstill on toughening trade legislation while it is negotiating entry to the World Trade Organisation (WTO), trade diplomats said.
The diplomats said the call was made by the United States, the European Union, Japan and Canada at a meeting of the WTO's working party studying the Russian application to join the 130-member body.

A senior EU official told the meeting, attended by a Moscow delegation headed by Deputy External Economic Relations Minister Georgy Gabuniya, that Russia should take "no new trade restrictive measures" while talks were under way, they said.
The call was echoed by Assistant U.S. Trade Representative Dorothy Dwoskin, who said Moscow "should move towards consistency with the rules of this house (the WTO)," according to the diplomats.

A Japanese trade official told the meeting, the fifth of the working group since Russia first applied to join the international trade club in 1993, that Tokyo attached "great importance" to a standstill, they added.

Trade envoys said no direct reference was made at the meeting to an appeal by President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday for Russian to buy home-produced goods. Yeltsin said his government would not use administrative means to limit imports.
